name: Kafr Qasem Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Kastner, Meir, Sandler & Dachkovsky (2014) on emergent structure in KQSL per Glottolog; no description of word stress/prosodic prominence located; sign language

sources.citation: Jaraisy, Marah & Rose Stamp. 2022. The Vulnerability of Emerging Sign Languages: (E)merging Sign Languages? Languages 7(1):49 (MDPI, open access).
sources.note: Most recent dedicated KQSL paper; open access but MDPI blocked automated download; would confirm whether any phonological/prosodic description of KQSL beyond Kastner et al. exists (background section, references).

sources.citation: Kastner, Itamar, Irit Meir, Wendy Sandler & Svetlana Dachkovsky. 2014. The emergence of embedded structure: insights from Kafr Qasem Sign Language. Frontiers in Psychology 5:525, 1-15. doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2014.00525
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing on word/sign-level stress. 'Prosodic analysis' (pp. 5-6) lists only phrase-level cues used to find constituent/intonational-phrase boundaries: pause or hold, change in body position, change in head position, lengthened duration/increased size of the constituent-final sign, spread of facial expression; notes clause-final position is 'prosodically prominent' (p. 7) and that utterance-final signs 'tend to be longer and bigger' (citing Nespor & Sandler 1999 on ISL).

sources.citation: Sandler, Wendy, et al. (Haifa Sign Language Research Lab) unpublished/in-prep KQSL corpus descriptions cited in Kastner et al. 2014 as 'Meir et al. (in preparation)' on KQSL word order.
